name: intel 8051 multiply from memory
desc: A simple example of multiplying two numbers stored in memory using the Intel 8051 microcontroller. The program multiplies two numbers located at memory addresses 8600H and 8601H, and stores the result in memory addresses 8700H (higher byte) and 8701H (lower byte).

files.sketch.ino:
MOV DPTR, #8600H    ; Point DPTR to first input address
MOVX A, @DPTR       ; Move first number into Accumulator A
MOV B, A            ; Move first number into Register B

MOV DPTR, #8601H    ; Point DPTR to second input address
MOVX A, @DPTR       ; Move second number into Accumulator A

MUL AB              ; Multiply A and B (A x B -> B:A)

MOV DPTR, #8701H    ; Point DPTR to lower byte result address
MOVX @DPTR, A       ; Save lower byte (from A)

MOV DPTR, #8700H    ; Point DPTR to higher byte result address
MOV A, B            ; Move higher byte into A
MOVX @DPTR, A       ; Save higher byte (from B)

HERE: SJMP HERE     ; Stop program execution
